fine_trace.code: FormField *Form::createFieldFromDict (Object &&obj, PDFDoc *docA, const Ref aref, FormField *parent, std::set<int> *usedParents)
fine_trace.note: The field dictionary Object parsed from the attacker-controlled PDF (AcroForm/Widget annotation dict) becomes a program value used to build the FormField tree; obj wraps a Dict whose ownership will be handed off without a matching reference for every place that retains it.

A raw Dict* is pulled out of the parsed Object without calling dict->incRef(); the FormField (and its children/parent linkage created below) subsequently treat this pointer as if it owned its own reference, so the safety obligation that every independent holder of the Dict increments its refcount is violated.
Child form fields are constructed and linked to the same parent/dict identity via std::move, propagating the under-referenced Dict pointer down the field tree without correcting the missing incRef.

fine_trace.code: delete rootFields[i]; // destroys FormField tree, unref'ing the shared Dict
fine_trace.note: During destruction of the standalone form's field tree, each FormField destructor decrements the Dict's reference count; because the earlier extraction at line 636 never incremented it, the cumulative decRef calls drop the refcount below the number of increments, producing an extra unref and a crash from the resulting insufficient/negative reference count.
